candidates.name: Hierarchical cohort-precision weighting of the fund leg (age x settlement-interval x liquidity tier, empirical-Bayes shrunk, judged maximin over years)
candidates.mechanism: The fund leg applies one cross-sectional mapping (rank of HL3d funding EMA) to every name, but the project's own measurements show the funding->return mapping is strongly heteroskedastic across name cohorts: listing age <90d carries IC 0.088/0.025/0.086 vs old 0.006/0.016/0.024 (2024/25/26), i.e. in the WORST year (2024) essentially all fund alpha sat in ~15 young names; names moved to 4h/1h settlement carry 2.6x larger 8h-equivalent funding (RESULT_xregime s1) and are the persistent extremes; liquidity tiers differ in adverse selection. When signal-to-noise differs by cohort, the Bayes-optimal linear combination is precision weighting: position_i = z_i * (IC_hat_c(i) / IC_hat_pooled), with cohort IC_hat estimated causally on a trailing 2-year window and shrunk (James-Stein / partial pooling) toward the pooled IC so that small cells cannot chase noise. This is the opposite of a focusing loss: no sample is dropped and no era is upweighted; it re-sizes positions by an estimate that uses ALL anchors of ALL years. It is also the opposite of the dead de-concentration family: it concentrates INTO the cohorts where the alpha is, consistent with the receipt that concentration is the alpha. C1 in PREREG_allweather (a fixed indicator tilt 1[age<90d], a in {0,.5,1,2}) is the one-cell, un-shrunk special case; this candidate is its superset and should run after C1 reads (a=0 / all multipliers=1 must reproduce baseline bitwise).
candidates.new_information_or_mechanism: New mechanism (statistical, acts on the 77% leg): cohort-level precision weighting with empirical-Bayes shrinkage, cohort = listing age x settlement interval x liquidity tier. No new data source; uses panel meta already on pod/jpline (listing date from first finite qvk/y4 anchor per E-0903-E; settlement interval column already in the panel; 4h quote-volume tier).
candidates.why_not_covered_by_closed_list: Fund-leg construction axis (A1-A5, impulse arms) tested FILTERS on the funding series (EMA half-life, settlement-space EMA, momentum/gap mixes) -- same mapping for all names; it never tested cohort-dependent sizing. Universe work tested age as a GATE (A7 free, A14/A30/A60 monotonically worse) not as a weight; PREREG_allweather C1 explicitly records 'age dimension not yet tested as weighting' and tests only a single fixed indicator. Concentration-cap / de-correlation receipts (N8/N9/mirror pairs) kill de-concentration; this concentrates. The feature-family ceiling (+0.0029 IC) applies to the MODEL leg's inputs, not to sizing inside the fund leg, which has 3-6x the book leverage of the model legs.
candidates.sample_arithmetic: Cells: 2 age x 3 settlement x 3 liquidity = 18 max; collapse to >=6 cells with >=20 names/anchor. Cohort IC SE over a 2-year trailing window ~ (1/sqrt(20))/sqrt(4380) ~ 0.0034; observed cohort spread 0.006 vs 0.088 is ~20 SE, so cohort ICs are estimable and shrinkage only matters for thin cells. Young names per anchor: 15 (2024) / 44 (2025) / 18 (2026) -> capacity is the binding constraint in 2024, not statistics: with per-name caps and the 250k qv4h floor, at most ~10-20% of gross can move into young cohorts. Book-level: fund leg ~1.2 bps/anchor/gross at old-cohort IC ~0.02; shifting 10-15% of gross into cohorts with ~3x IC gives roughly +0.1 to +0.2 bps/anchor gross, minus ~half for wider spreads/higher turnover in young names -> net +0.05 to +0.10; paired-Delta SE in the w10 chain is ~0.02-0.03 pooled 2023+ and ~0.05 per year, so a +0.08 effect is detectable pooled and borderline per-year. Regime check: effect should be LARGEST in 2024 (young 0.088 vs old 0.006) -- so read maximin over years, not mean.
candidates.minimal_test: CPU replay only, ~5 h. (1) Build causal cohort labels per name-anchor on the pod v2ext panel (age from first finite qvk/y4 anchor; settlement interval column; liquidity tercile of trailing-30d median qv4h). (2) Causal cohort-IC estimator: trailing 2-year Spearman(fund z, y4) per cell, shrunk m_c = 1 + lambda_c*(IC_c/IC_pool - 1), lambda_c = n_c/(n_c + n0) with n0 in {2k, 10k} rows; multipliers clipped to [0.5, 3]. (3) w10 chain patch COHW (fund z * m_c, re-normalised inside the rank base like C1), identity assertion COHW=off -> bitwise baseline; arms: C1 best-a (for reference), COHW-age-only, COHW-age x settle, COHW-full, two seeds. (4) Judge: live form (M829/T400/FTRIM, dynamic seat, CAL=log, real fees), paired Delta net_ex 2024->26 CI, PLUS maximin: worst-year Delta and worst-year Sharpe; turnover <= +15%; report young/short-settle notional share (capacity) and per-cohort realised net-of-cost so that 'IC positive but net zero' (five cases on record) is caught. Kill-switch at 1 h: if per-cohort trailing IC estimates are unstable year-to-year (sign flips in >2 cells) stop.
candidates.regime_helped: Low-dispersion / narrow-breadth years (2024-type) where old-cohort fund IC ~0 but young/short-settlement cohorts still carry alpha; roughly neutral to mildly positive in 2026-type years; does nothing for broad-rally loss anchors.

candidates.name: Covariate-shift importance weighting for king (adversarial-validation density ratio on anchor-state, ESS-floored) = test-time adaptation without a regime indicator
candidates.mechanism: Instead of re-weighting training anchors by OUTCOME (worst-era DRO, which is what L1SM/B1 do and what collapses effective sample), re-weight them by INPUT similarity to the current deployment window. At each monthly retrain date t, fit a classifier on a 12-dim anchor-level state vector (cross-sectional sigma of funding, share of negative-funding names, qualified-name count, median 7d vol, BTC 30d return, funding percentile, N_eff proxy, etc.) distinguishing anchors in [t-60d, t) from all anchors < t; convert to density-ratio weights w = clip(p_cur/p_hist, 0.2, 5), normalise, and enforce ESS >= 50% of anchors. Train the production LightGBM king recipe with sample_weight = w (constant within an anchor). Mechanism: the king mapping is currently fit with gradient mass dominated by 2025-26 (more names, 3x dispersion); when the state drifts back toward a 2024-like configuration, the weights automatically shift mass to 2023-24-like anchors -- adaptation happens in the training set, with no gross timing and no regime forecast (sigma_fund is ~random walk, so the 'current value' IS the best predictor, which is exactly what this uses). Under the corrected caliber the dynamic seat gives king 0.64/0.67 in 2024/25 (RESULT_caliber_revalidation table), so model-side changes have ~0.35x book leverage in weak years, not the 0.21x quoted from the old caliber.
candidates.new_information_or_mechanism: New mechanism: input-distribution (covariate-shift) importance weighting with an explicit effective-sample floor. Distinct from outcome-based era weighting (L1SM, B1), from feeding regime context as features (R1CTX, no gain), from retrain cadence (K1-K3), and from seat rules R1-R5. Free data; the K1 monthly harness on pod (pod_king_rolling_monthly.py, 32 folds in 1042 s) already exists and only needs a sample_weight argument.
candidates.why_not_covered_by_closed_list: R1CTX added regime context as DL inputs (no gain) -- a tree can in principle learn interactions from context features but that is a different inductive path from re-weighting the fit; L1SM/B1 re-weight by worst-era OUTCOME (and B1's own prior notes seat cap); K1-K3 change cadence (freshness) not the sample distribution; R5 conditions the SEAT on sigma_fund tercile (UNDECIDED) not the model fit; 'regime timing 5 forms' acted on gross. Honest caveat that limits this candidate: K1 raised king OOS IC ~9% in 2024-25 and the book did not move (RESULT_rolling_king_monthly), so king-IC->book transfer is near zero at current costs; this candidate only pays if the weak-year IC gain is materially larger than K1's and/or comes with lower turnover.
candidates.sample_arithmetic: Anchors 2022-2026 ~10k (3.5M name-rows). Weights constant within anchor, ESS floor 5k anchors -> at most 2x sample shrinkage (vs 3-5x for R5 focusing). Yearly king IC SE ~ 0.06/sqrt(2190) * 1.5 (autocorr) ~ 0.002; a +0.005 (8%) weak-year IC change is detectable at the score layer (t~2.5). Book: king leg raw ~2.6 bps/anchor at IC ~0.06 (RESULT_retrain_cadence R2 line) -> ~0.4 bps per 0.01 IC at leg level; +0.005 IC -> +0.2 leg -> x0.35 seat (weak years) -> ~+0.07 book, but the K1 receipt says the realised transfer at +0.005 IC was ~0, so the honest expectation is +0.00 to +0.05 in weak years only. Paired per-year SE ~0.05 -> the test can only reject 'nothing', not confirm +0.03.
candidates.minimal_test: ~4 h, CPU (LightGBM) or GPU-optional. Step 0 (30 min, kill-switch): adversarial-validation AUC of 60-day-window vs history on the 12-dim anchor state; if AUC < 0.6 there is no exploitable covariate shift -> stop and report. Step 1: density-ratio weights per anchor (logistic or uLSIF), clip [0.2,5], ESS >= 50%; print ESS per fold. Step 2: K1 harness (pod retrain_2026-09/rolling_king_2026-09-05/pod_king_rolling_monthly.py) with sample_weight, identity assertion w=1 -> bitwise K1 preds; 32 monthly folds x 2 arms (clip 5 / clip 2) x 2 seeds ~ 1.5 h. Step 3: judge.py per-year IC (raw y4 and Pi target) + book replay via pod_king_ic_legs.py / w10 live form (CAL=log, dynamic seat and W3FIX 0.30), paired Delta per year; gate = worst-year Delta CI lower bound > 0 and 2026 Delta >= -0.05 and turnover <= +10%.
candidates.regime_helped: Only 2023-24-type low-dispersion years, and only through the model seat (~0.35x); ~0 in 2026-type years.

candidates.name: Era-balanced / group-DRO sample weights for king (year-equal weights, worst-year softmax with ESS floor) plus maximin hyperparameter selection -- the king-side complement of Track B's B1
candidates.mechanism: King's training set is dominated by 2025-26 rows (457 qualified names vs 185 in 2023; 3x dispersion), so the fitted mapping is tuned to the high-dispersion era. Two cheap re-weightings keep every sample and only re-balance eras: (a) year-equal weights (each year's rows sum to the same weight; 2023 rows up-weighted ~2.4x, ESS drop ~25%); (b) group-DRO over half-year blocks implemented as outer-loop softmax weights w_e ~ exp(-mean_net_e/T) recomputed between short boosting rounds with an ESS >= 50% floor (temperature T large enough that no block gets > 3x its equal weight). Model selection is switched from mean-over-folds IC to min-over-year-folds IC (Numerai-style era consistency), which changes what is chosen without touching the objective. Rationale for a positive rather than zero prior: B1 does this for V2MAIN only (45% of the model seat); king (55%) is untouched, and under the corrected caliber the model seat in weak years is 0.64-0.67, so king-side weak-year improvements have ~0.35x leverage.
candidates.new_information_or_mechanism: Mechanism transfer: era-balanced / DRO weighting applied to the LightGBM king (never done; L1SM and B1 are V2MAIN-only) with an explicit ESS floor so the effective sample cannot collapse the way R5 focusing did; plus maximin fold selection.
candidates.why_not_covered_by_closed_list: L1SM (half-year SoftMin on V2MAIN, REJECT 09-02) and B1 (in flight) are DL-objective arms; king was never era-balanced. 'Focusing losses' (R5) are per-sample outcome weights that shrink effective sample 3-5x; year-equal weighting shrinks ESS ~25% and DRO here is ESS-floored. K1-K3 changed cadence, not weights. Caveat honestly stated: king year-fold OOS IC is already flat (0.056-0.062 by year, ic_canon_table), which argues the mapping is not badly era-tuned and the expected gain is small; and the K1 receipt (IC +9% -> book 0) bounds the transfer.
candidates.sample_arithmetic: Blocks: 9 half-year blocks 2022H1-2026H1; year-equal weights ESS ~ 0.75 n; DRO with T chosen so max block weight <= 3x equal -> ESS >= 0.5 n by construction. Score layer: per-year IC SE ~0.002, so a weak-year gain of +0.004 is at t~2; multiple comparisons: 2 weightings x 2 seeds x 1 selection rule = 4 arms, Bonferroni-adjusted resolution ~+0.005 IC. Book: same transfer as candidate 2 (~0.35x seat in weak years, K1 receipt says realised transfer ~0 at +0.005 IC) -> honest +0.00 to +0.04 bps/anchor weak-year.
candidates.minimal_test: ~2.5 h incremental on candidate 2's harness (same pod K1 script, sample_weight path, identity assertion). Arms: YEQ (year-equal), DRO-T (T in {large}, ESS floor printed per fold), each x 2 seeds; selection: report both mean-fold and min-fold IC and pick by min-fold. Judge identical to candidate 2 (per-year IC both targets; live-form book replay CAL=log dynamic seat + W3FIX 0.30; gate worst-year Delta CI > 0, 2026 Delta >= -0.05, turnover <= +10%). Kill-switch: if YEQ moves 2024/2025 fold IC by < +0.002, DRO arm is not run.
candidates.regime_helped: 2023-24-type years via the model seat; neutral or slightly negative in 2026-type years (mass shifted away from the dominant era).

candidates.name: Imbalance-conditioned posting: actioning the E2 reversal with L1 queue sizes from the executor's own pricing snapshot
candidates.mechanism: Textbook maker adverse selection: a resting post-only order fills either because the mid drifts toward it (benign fill, price then reverts) or because an informed market order sweeps the queue at its level (toxic fill, price continues). Which of the two happens is largely predictable one tick ahead from L1 queue imbalance (bidQty vs askQty). Live receipt RESULT-E2 (docs/DESIGN_lob_shortcycle_2026-08-26.md): when the near-book is aligned with our side, filled markout60 = -6.3 to -6.4 bps; when the book is against us, +0.8 to +1.6 bps; separation 7-8 bps at 4-5 sigma, total maker markout -2.41 bps. Policy: for each name at submit, if imbalance is against us (queue on the opposite side heavier, mid likely to move to us) post-only join immediately; if aligned (mid likely to move away, any fill is a sweep), do not post at the touch: re-check every ~10 s and post when the imbalance flips, otherwise fall to the existing window-end path. This converts the currently random mix of benign/toxic fills into a selected subset. The executor already fetches one universe-wide /fapi/v1/ticker/bookTicker at the anchor (binance_executor.py L477-480) which returns bestBidQty/bestAskQty; it uses price and spread only. Zero extra venue calls.
candidates.new_information_or_mechanism: NEW INFORMATION: bestBidQty/bestAskQty for all ~450 names at the pricing snapshot (already in the response the executor consumes, never stored or used); the E2 reading came from a 12-band LOB recorder covering ~20% of fills (80% dropped for missing bands, selection bias unresolved). NEW MECHANISM: reverse of E2's preregistered hypothesis (delay/step back when the book is aligned, post freely when against), which the E2 record explicitly says may be revived only with a reversed hypothesis, a longer sample and a tick-level reconstruction gate.
candidates.why_not_covered_by_closed_list: Closed list covers factor/model/book construction, execution RL, chase (post-run top-up), and the placement bandit's existing join/behind/exempt arms. E2 was closed 'by gate' because the sign of the effect was preset the wrong way, not because the information was found useless; the receipt itself lists the revival conditions. LOB depth as a 4h direction factor is dead, but this is a seconds-horizon placement decision, a different quantity at a different horizon. The behind-arm receipt (markout -7.69 vs join -2.40, RESULT_requote_and_behind 2026-09-05) is consistent with, not contrary to, this mechanism (more passive = more toxic).
candidates.sample_arithmetic: Unit of observation is the order, not the anchor. Last 29 days: 24,421 attempt-1 maker orders (~840/day) + 9,065 top-ups. Per-fill markout60 sd ~27 bps (E2). Randomised 50/50 arm on all attempt-1 maker orders for 14 days: ~5,900 orders/arm; SE of the ITT all-in-cost difference (sd ~40 bps incl. residual handling) = 40*sqrt(2/5900) = 0.74 bps/unit; a 1.5 bps/unit effect is 2 sigma in 2 weeks, 2.8 sigma in 4 weeks. Only ~45% of orders are in the aligned state, so the policy effect on the all-order mean is 0.45 x (toxic->benign delta 4-5 bps) ~= +1.9 bps/unit on fills before the fill-rate penalty. Detectable. The book-level translation is tiny: 0.5-0.8 bps/unit turnover x 5% = 0.025-0.04 bps/anchor/gross; at the live target-vector turnover of 1.77%/anchor (84 anchors, sum|dw|/2) it is 0.009-0.014.
candidates.minimal_test: Step 1 (1-2 h, non-book-behaviour, safe_commit + battery): persist bidQty/askQty/imbalance from the pricing bookTicker into orders.jsonl per order. Step 2 (offline, 0 GPU, after 3-5 days of logging, ~2 h): replicate the E2 split on the full order set with L1 imbalance only (join fills, markout60 with the now near-full backfill coverage); gate: aligned-vs-against markout gap >= 3 bps with CI excluding 0 on n >= 2,000 fills. Step 3 (4 h build): contextual arm in the existing placement bandit (arms unchanged, imbalance as context; 'wait-on-aligned' vs current), deterministic hash split, 14-day readout, primary = plan-level ITT all-in cost vs mid_at_anchor with the existing analyse_requote_behind.py caliber, cluster by UTC day. Schedule after the requote readout (>= 09-19) or exclude -5022 plans from the denominator to avoid contaminating that experiment.

candidates.name: Settlement-straddle execution: cut paying positions and add receiving positions before the funding snapshot, everything else after
candidates.mechanism: Funding is paid on the position held at the settlement instant, not pro-rata. The executor reads the target at N+24 min, so every anchor at a settlement time (now 00/04/08/12/16/20Z for most names: 22,038 of 29,028 ledger rows are 4h-interval, 6,307 8h, 681 1h) trades AFTER the snapshot. That is optimal for cuts of receiving positions and adds of paying positions, and wrong for the other two categories: a paying position that the new target reduces pays one more full settlement before being cut; a receiving position that the target increases misses one settlement. On this book's own target vectors (86 target_live files 2026-08-20 -> 09-05, weights per unit gross, rates from ~/wide_shadow/state/aux.json ledger_tail): book funding = -1.51 +/- 0.07 bps/anchor/gross (the book PAYS; venue ledger says -1.9), receiving-side add turnover 0.46%/anchor, and executing paying-cuts before the snapshot recovers +0.027 +/- 0.004 bps/anchor/gross, receiving-adds +0.003 (4h-interval names +0.002, 8h +0.001); total +0.030 bps/anchor/gross = +0.65%/gross/yr = ~+1.3% NAV/yr at 2x, uniform across anchor hours (0.020-0.034). Policy: at S-10 min run a provisional target (fund leg from the venue's premiumIndex lastFundingRate, which is the rate that will settle at S and is >90% determined by then; model legs from the S-4h scores through the EMA), execute only the two 'before' categories, then the normal pass at S+24 against the true target.

candidates.name: Vesting / unlock calendar as a hedging-pressure identifier for the fund leg (DefiLlama free static emissions dataset)
candidates.mechanism: Token vesting schedules are public, dated years in advance, and recipients (VCs, teams, market makers) hedge upcoming cliffs by shorting the perp 1-4 weeks ahead (Keyrock, an OTC/MM desk, states this explicitly: 'most firms, including ours, start hedging 1-2 weeks or even a month before'). That hedging drives the funding rate negative for a reason that has nothing to do with the leveraged-flow state the fund leg is designed to harvest: the fund leg goes LONG the most negative-funding names, so pre-cliff it is systematically long tokens with a scheduled supply dump, collecting the hedgers' carry while bearing the pre-unlock drift (Keyrock: ~90% of 16k unlocks negative, decline starts ~30d before and accelerates in the final week; team cliffs worst, ecosystem/foundation cliffs ~+1%). After the cliff the hedges are unwound (short covering) and the drift reverses over ~2 weeks. Three usable forms: (a) size-weighted 'unlock % of circulating within next 30d' as a long-side downweight/exclusion inside the fund leg; (b) post-cliff 0-14d hedge-unwind window as a long-side upweight; (c) linear daily emission rate (unlocksPerDay / circSupply) as a slow, low-turnover cross-sectional state (continuous dilution). The dataset also gives float ratio at TGE and days-to-first-cliff, which lets the untested young-listing age effect be separated from float/unlock structure.

NEW MECHANISM: conditioning the fund leg on the CAUSE of negative funding (scheduled hedging pressure vs leveraged flow) rather than on the funding series itself; all closed funding features (term structure, vol, percentile, momentum, cumulative, cross-venue) are functions of the funding path alone.

candidates.name: Delta-neutral funding-carry sleeve on idle collateral (long spot / short perp on top-predicted-funding names; BTC/ETH quarterly basis as low-risk floor)
candidates.mechanism: The book is a perp-only cross-sectional position that uses ~10-15% of NAV as margin at 2x gross; 70-80% of NAV sits idle as USDT. A cash-and-carry sleeve (long spot, short the same perp) has zero price exposure and earns the funding that crowded longs pay. Its income is concentrated in bull/leverage-driven regimes with high positive funding, which are the quarters where the funding-momentum book is weakest (24Q2 -9.3% at 2x while top-decile funding among 81 majors ran 2.15 bps/8h = 24% annualised; 2024H2 22-31%). In the book's rich regime (2025-26: funding pinned near the 1 bp/8h default, top-decile 1.0-1.1 bps/8h = 11%) the sleeve degrades to roughly a risk-free floor on idle collateral. Because the sleeve is price-neutral it does not give back the dominance premium (the failure mode of every beta/spread hedge in the receipts); it adds a second income stream with low correlation via the funding channel only. Predicted next funding (Binance premium-index TWAP) is known before settlement, so entry/exit is causal and the income is nearly deterministic; the risk is basis mark-to-market and spot fees.
candidates.new_information_or_mechanism: Spot market as a TRADED INSTRUMENT (not as a feature) plus Binance UM quarterly delivery contracts for basis; both never used in the project. Mechanism = delta-neutral carry harvest on idle collateral, a second P&L stream rather than a modification of the book's exposure.
candidates.why_not_covered_by_closed_list: Closed receipts cover (a) cross-venue funding differentials as a predictive feature (dead), (b) hedging the alt-BTC spread / BTC beta (destroys the premium because the hedge has negative expected return), (c) premium-sleeve budgeting inside the book. None applies: this adds a price-neutral leg with its own positive carry; it neither predicts Binance returns nor removes the book's spread exposure. PREREG_allweather_programme A1 uses spot data only as name-level features (spot/perp volume ratio, basis as a column), not as a traded sleeve. Ops precondition: spot collateral must live in Portfolio Margin / unified account so the executor's NAV and 4-5e guards see one equity.
candidates.sample_arithmetic: Income is observed every settlement (3/day): 2024-05 to 2026-08 local file = 6,121 settlements x 81 majors (VERIFIED: top-decile mean 2.03 bps/8h in 2024, 1.14 in 2025, 1.03 in 2026; 24Q4 2.84); full 829-name history 2020-> on jpline. Statistical power is not the constraint (funding income is near-deterministic; correlation with the book's 5,800 archived anchors has SE 0.013); the constraint is net-of-cost feasibility by year. candidates.name: Calendar-cell gross allocation: weekend anchors and the 16Z US-session anchor (pre-registered two cells, turnover-costed)
candidates.mechanism: External evidence says alts outperform BTC on weekends (daily 0.41% vs 0.19% for alts, 0.26% vs 0.14% for BTC/ETH; strongest in bull markets) and that weekend liquidity/commonality is thinner. The book has beta -0.25 per unit gross to the alt-minus-BTC spread; a +0.15%/day weekend spread drift implies weekend anchors earn roughly 0.6 bps/anchor/gross less than weekdays purely from the premium leg, while their variance is not lower. The FOMC pre-decision 16Z anchor already showed the calendar carries structure (-73 bps vs +5.4, placebo-clean). If weekend anchors (2/7 of all anchors) have mean <= ~0.3 bps, halving gross on them cuts ~21% of book variance at a cost of ~0.09 bps/anchor (2 x 50% gross traded per week at 3.9 bps), lifting Sharpe by roughly 0.1-0.2 with no signal change; if the weekend mean is as high as weekdays the arm loses (variance cut is outweighed by lost mean plus turnover) - the gate below encodes this.
candidates.new_information_or_mechanism: Calendar (weekday x anchor-of-day) as a causal gross dial - the only indicator that is causal by construction. New relative to the FOMC pass, which used a 36-event macro calendar; day-of-week has never been tested at book level (docs grep: only hour-of-day as a signal, 'p=0.012 real, +0.16 Sharpe upper bound, dominated by smoothing' - a signal-layer verdict that does not apply to a gross multiplier).
candidates.why_not_covered_by_closed_list: The five dead timing forms used return/trend/regime indicators ('no causal indicator'); a calendar is causal by definition and the same family (FOMC pre-shrink) is an open item with a positive prior. Hour-of-day was recorded as a signal-layer feature and absorbed by the EMA smoothing; gross scaling is multiplicative on the whole book and bypasses the smoothing. Not a drawdown/ladder trigger (no fast-cliff mechanism involved).
candidates.sample_arithmetic: 2024-01->2026-08 = ~5,800 anchors; weekend cell = ~1,650 anchors, per-anchor sigma 25.6 bps/gross -> SE of cell mean 0.63 bps; the hypothesised gap (weekend ~+0.6 vs weekday ~+1.4 bps) is 1.3 sigma of the difference SE (0.75) - marginal, so the frozen gate uses a one-sided t <= -2 on the cell vs complement plus same-sign in 3/3 years. 16Z weekday cell = ~830 anchors, SE 0.9 bps. lenses.notes: DIVERSIFICATION ARITHMETIC (script receipt: scratchpad/arith.py, run this session). (1) Sharpe sampling noise at 4h: SE(annualised Sharpe) = sqrt(2190/n) -> 90-day window SE 2.0, one year SE 1.0, 2.7 years SE 0.61. A true-Sharpe-2.2 process shows a 90-day 5th percentile of about -1.1 and 95th of 5.5 (observed -2.1 / 6.4), so most of the rolling-quarter dispersion is sampling noise on top of real regime dependence. 'Sharpe >= 3 in every 90-day window' requires true Sharpe >= 6.3; '>= 3 in 95% of years' requires true >= 4.6. No allocation change reaches that; the honest allocation goal is raising the floor (weak years 1.1-1.2 -> 1.5-1.8, worst week/maxDD) and the full-period Sharpe from 2.2 to ~2.5-2.7. (2) Second-book requirement, optimal weights, S = sqrt((S1^2+S2^2-2 rho S1 S2)/(1-rho^2)), target 3: with S1 = 2.2 -> rho 0 needs S2 2.04; rho -0.3 needs 1.29; rho -0.5 needs 0.67; rho -0.7 needs ~0 (a zero-Sharpe hedge at rho -0.7 alone gives 3.08 - but every spread/beta hedge tested has strongly negative Sharpe because it returns the premium, which is why hedges fail). With weak-year S1 = 1.1 -> rho 0 needs 2.79; rho -0.3 needs 2.33; rho -0.5 needs 1.87; rho -0.7 needs 1.22. No known second book meets these in weak years. Crowding that is financed only in the perp (perp taker-buy imbalance and OI rising while spot taker flow is flat or opposite) is fragile: it is the setup for the two loss shapes in RESULT_xregime - the 'L|P washout' (positive-funding longs collapsing, -445U in late Aug) and the deep-negative short squeeze (4h > +8% probability 5.0% vs 0.8%). Crowding accompanied by spot taker buying (real demand lifting the index price) persists and squeezes shorts through the index. Spot klines carry taker-buy base volume, so a name-level divergence D = spot taker-buy share - perp taker-buy share (and spot/perp volume ratio) is computable at 5m -> 4h for the ~350 of 450 names with Binance spot pairs. Use: multiplicative tilt on the fund leg's z by spot-support tercile (down-weight perp-only crowding on both sides), which by construction is low-correlated with the fund premium (it only reshapes within the leg's existing positions).
candidates.new_information_or_mechanism: New INFORMATION SOURCE: Binance SPOT 5m klines (data.binance.vision spot/, free; repo has zero spot usage on record, PREREG_allweather A1). New MECHANISM relative to A1's planned feature list: not a model feature through the S1 IC gate (seat <= 0.3x kills it) but a book-level conditioning of the 77% leg, tested as a replay tilt like FTRIM/M1 were.

The 8-family feature ceiling (+0.0029) measured model IC; this candidate is measured in leg-level book net like the fund-leg engineering arms (PREREG_fundleg's own scoping statement).

Structural reason it cannot reach 3: the book is a two-factor book (dominance premium 78% of mean at beta -0.25/gross; low-vol tilt 65% of net; N_eff ~3) with a Sharpe-0.6-0.8 residual; PREREG_allweather §0's own diversification arithmetic needs a second book with Sharpe ~3.1 at rho 0 to lift a weak-year 1.1 to 3, and the five lenses found no second premium above Sharpe ~0.5-1 (basis carry: floor-only, correlated with the hot regime; TSMOM/options: undetectable). Track C's frontier of 51 archived definitions tops out at worst-year Sharpe 1.70 with +-0.3 seed noise; no archived arm has worst-year >= 2. The deepest all-weather risk (the fund mapping's sign flipped from reversal in 2021-22 to continuation in 2024-26) has exactly one transition in history, so no switching rule can be validated; the only honest instrument is the live dual-engine monitor plus the per-name stop. Measurability: SE(annualised Sharpe | 1 year) ~1.0, | 90 days ~2.0, | 2024-26 ~0.62 (Lo 2002); a true Sharpe-3-everywhere book would still show a 90-day Sharpe < 0 in ~5-7% of quarters and a year < 1.35 in 5% of years, so 'realised >= 3 in every regime' is unattainable for any strategy at this sigma. Restate the target as expected net per unit gross conditional on the regime dictionary with SE, and as P(negative year) = Phi(-Sharpe): the programme can plausibly move the weak-regime expected Sharpe from ~1.2 to ~1.5-1.8 (P(negative year) 11.5% -> 4-7%), not to 3.
